hypotheses.description: AI-assisted writing sounds more like own unassisted writing after post-editing than before.
Post-edited text sounds more like the author's OWN unassisted writing than like OTHER participants' unassisted writing.
hypotheses.comparison: edited->own control  vs  edited->other participants' control

hypotheses.description: AI-assisted writing sounds LESS like LLM-generated writing after post-editing than before (LUAR style measure; paper also uses PANGRAM).
Post-edited writing still sounds MORE like LLM-generated writing than like the author's own unassisted writing.
Post-edited writing is MORE stylistically homogeneous (higher between-author similarity) than unassisted human writing.
hypotheses.comparison: between-author similarity: control pairs  vs  edited pairs

hypotheses.description: Post-edited writing is LESS stylistically homogeneous than LLM-generated writing.
hypotheses.comparison: between-author similarity: draft pairs  vs  edited pairs

hypotheses.description: After post-editing, participants sound LESS like their own unassisted writing than like OTHER participants' post-edited writing.
hypotheses.comparison: edited->own control  vs  edited->other participants' edited

H3.description: Participants' perceived self-similarity agrees with the LUAR style metric (repeated-measures correlation over the draft and edited text of each treatment task).
H3.comparison: perceived self-similarity (capture+friend, 1-5)  vs  LUAR similarity to own control

caveats: Scores are treated as independent; tasks are nested within participants and homogeneity pairs reuse participants.
LLM style class = other participants' drafts (leave-own-participant-out).
H1b uses the LUAR style measure only; PANGRAM scores are not available in this dataset.
Control writing is represented by one combined embedding per participant, matching the paper's one-point-per-participant homogeneity analysis.
